title: Claim
description: Schema for Claim objects — explicit analytical propositions of the thesis. A Claim is a workspace-layer object. When validated, it can be promoted to a graph entity of type 'AnalyticClaim' (already defined in v96 types, zero instances as of 2026-04-04) via a versioned patch.

id.description: Unique identifier (32-char hex or human-readable slug for workspace objects)

name.description: Short label for the claim. Used as display name if promoted to graph entity.

claimText.description: Full analytical proposition text. Must be a complete sentence making a substantive claim.

claimType.description: Category of claim. 'central' = main thesis argument. 'subsidiary' = supporting argument. 'methodological' = claim about research method. 'contested' = claim that is explicitly debated.

confidence.description: Author's confidence level in this claim.

chapter.description: Primary thesis chapter where this claim is made.

thesisLocation.description: Human-readable location of the claim in the thesis.

sectionKey.description: Machine-readable ThesisSection key (matches ThesisSection entity names in canonical graph).

supportingQuoteIds.description: IDs of SourceQuote entities (in canonical graph) that support this claim.

supportingEntityIds.description: IDs of graph entities that provide supporting evidence or context for this claim.

contestingEntityIds.description: IDs of entities or claims that contest or complicate this claim.

parentClaimId.description: ID of the parent claim (for subsidiary claims). Enables hierarchical argument structure.

author.description: Author or agent that created this claim record.

promotedToEntityId.description: If promoted to canonical graph entity (AnalyticClaim type), the resulting entity ID.

notes.description: Free-text notes about this claim, its evidence, or open questions.

examples.name: Bitcoin is not reducible to its protocol
examples.claimText: Bitcoin cannot be reduced to its technical protocol specification; it is constituted through the ongoing governance practices, crises, and social negotiations of its community.
examples.author: mael-rolland.eth

examples.name: CVE-2018 reveals a closed-door governance mode
examples.claimText: The CVE-2018-17144 vulnerability disclosure reveals a discrete, non-public mode of governance in Bitcoin that contradicts the ideology of radical transparency.
examples.thesisLocation: Chapitre III > Gouvernance discrète dévoilée par les crises
examples.author: mael-rolland.eth
